root.claim: A single deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine computes the exact product of two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: reduce multiplication through radix digits, a CRT address map, Gaussian resampling and a coefficient twist to convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, accelerate its address moves and butterfly layers with two tape procedures derived from finite linear networks with a rank saving, recover the product exactly, and balance the parameters

motivation.text: Scanning $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so both data movement and butterfly arithmetic must each save a power of the logarithm.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

$m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: The source Fourier transform on pairwise coprime axes factors through Gaussian contractions and a power-of-two transform whose target permutation is absorbed by a chirp, and whose source permutation cancels in convolution.
children.method: apply Gaussian resampling with both coordinate permutations kept in the identity, take tensor products over axes, convert the middle transform by Bluestein's chirp, and let the source permutation cancel

motivation.text: Sorting twice on each coordinate would cost full passes, so keeping both permutations in the formula avoids them.

coordinate. We retain both permutations in the transform formula and
compute that formula directly.
